The book refines this by specifying the NAME as the impressed inscription (e.g., ' HOLINESS TO THE LORD') and linking it explicitly to the law as frontlets, while retaining the protective stamping by the Spirit and contrast with the counterfeit mark. 2 Timothy 2:19 is central to both, and the priestly context adds precision without replacing the ownership/protection symbolism.

The book narrows the seal to the specific NAME impressed (priestly plate and law) and its dual inscription (ownership and moral separation), excluding broader alternatives like Sabbath observance or purely sacramental baptism in favor of this engraved name motif.
